rd.open.dilemma: It seems that what weighs on you is not the lack of a clear reason to choose, but the presence of real reasons pulling in both directions.
rd.open.deciding: It seems that the hesitation here is less about missing information and more about the weight of the decision itself; the closer something is to your life and your future, the heavier and slower the choice becomes.
rd.open.harm: It seems that what you are living through is not an ordinary disagreement, but harm that keeps recurring and touches your dignity and your safety; so any thought about the next step begins with your right to be safe.
rd.open.power: It seems that this situation holds two pains at once: the pain of the injustice itself, and the pain of being unable to answer it when it comes from someone who holds power over you. That combination is what makes silence heavy and speaking frightening at the same time.
rd.open.anxious: It seems that the worry here lives in the future more than in the present; the mind runs ahead of the event and lives it many times before it happens, enlarging what might happen as much as it shrinks your ability to deal with it.
rd.open.sad: It seems that what you carry is a real weight even if it has no single clear cause; sadness does not always need a specific event to be genuine, and sometimes it is the sum of small things that piled up quietly.
rd.open.lonely: It seems that what you miss is not having people around you so much as having someone who notices you and asks about you; a person can be among many and still feel unseen.
rd.open.wronged: It seems that what hurts you is not only what happened, but what it means to you: that it came from someone you did not expect it from, or in a way that touches your dignity and your sense of fairness.
rd.open.grieving: It seems that what you are going through is not passing sadness, but a loss that rearranges many things inside you; absence does not take the person alone, it also takes the habits, conversations and roles that were part of your day.
rd.open.erred: It seems that what occupies you is not only the mistake, but what comes after it: how to mend what broke, and how to look at yourself after what happened. That concern itself is a sign of a living conscience.
rd.open.carer: It seems that you are carrying more than your words show: the practical load of caregiving, a silent worry for someone you love, and perhaps a feeling that your tiredness goes unseen.
rd.open.worried: It seems that your worry comes from love more than anything else; you are thinking about someone who matters to you, and trying to see what may come before it comes.
rd.open.burden: It seems that what you wrote describes not a single situation so much as an accumulation: pressure that went on until tiredness became part of your day.
rd.open.self: It seems that the difficulty here lies not only in the situation, but in how it reflects on the picture you have of yourself; what happens outside quickly turns into a verdict inside.
rd.open.ghurba: It seems that what you are living abroad is not only distance from a place, but distance from a version of yourself that lived among its people, its language and its small details; that is why homesickness sometimes comes as a tiredness whose source you cannot name.
rd.open.transition: It seems that what you are going through is a time of transition more than a single problem; change takes away the familiar before it offers a replacement, and between the two lies a stretch of confusion that is entirely natural.
rd.open.emergency: It seems that this happened suddenly and left the mark of shock before anything else; in moments like these thinking narrows and worry speeds up, and that is a natural reaction, not a weakness.
rd.open.digital: It seems that what happened in the digital world has left a mark beyond the screen: a feeling of exposure, or of losing control over what belongs to you, and that feeling is real and understandable.
rd.open.boundaries: It seems that the difficulty here is not the request itself, but saying “no” to the person asking; refusing often feels like harshness or loss, even when it is a legitimate protection of your time and energy.
rd.open.work: It seems that what you are living at work goes beyond the tasks themselves to what touches your sense of appreciation, fairness and stability; and these things seep into home and sleep more than we expect.
rd.open.money: It seems that the financial strain here is not limited to numbers, but extends to the sense of security and the ability to plan, and perhaps to embarrassment in front of others.
rd.open.conflict: It seems that the conflict here is not only about the visible topic, but about what lies beneath it: a need for appreciation, for words to be heard and understood, or for a sense of safety in the relationship.
rd.open.parenting: It seems that what occupies you in raising your children goes beyond the behaviour itself to searching for the right way; that concern alone is a sign of real care, not of failing.
rd.open.faith: It seems that what occupies you touches your relationship with Allah and how you see yourself before Him; that concern itself is evidence of a living heart seeking closeness, not of a distant one.
rd.open.health: It seems that the illness here touches not only the body, but the sense of safety and of control over the details of daily life, and with it comes an understandable worry about what lies ahead.
rd.open.habit: It seems that what you describe is a repeating cycle more than a single mistake: distress that pushes toward the habit, then regret that brings the distress back; understanding this cycle helps more than blaming yourself for it.
rd.open.general: It seems that there is more in your words than appears in their first lines; behind the visible situation are feelings and needs that deserve to be understood before any solution is sought.

rd.pullsOnly: What draws you toward this choice is clear: {0}; and perhaps what delays the decision is not the weakness of these reasons, but the size of what follows from it.

rd.option.accept_refuse: Accepting may mean coming closer to what you feel at ease with, yet it also opens questions about stability and the responsibilities ahead; refusing may seem safer, yet it may carry a fear of losing something that may not come again. So each option becomes tied to a possible loss, not only to a clear gain.
rd.option.stay_leave: Staying may mean preserving what you have built and the stability of those around you, yet it may also mean that what exhausts you continues; leaving may hold a promise of relief, yet it also carries fear of the unknown and of the cost of separation. Perhaps the difficulty is that both paths have a real cost.
rd.option.forgive_cut: Forgiving may mean peace of heart and keeping a bond that has value, yet it may raise a fear that the harm will be repeated; cutting ties may feel like self-protection, yet it may leave an emptiness or a sense of guilt. It matters that forgiveness does not necessarily mean returning to how things were.
rd.option.speak_silent: Speaking openly may mean doing justice to yourself and bringing clarity to the relationship, yet it carries fear of the reaction and of what might change between you; staying silent may keep the peace for now, yet it may pile up inside you what is hard to carry for long.
rd.option.move_stay: Moving may mean a chance for a wider beginning, yet it also means leaving the familiar and those close to you; staying keeps closeness and security, yet it may leave a question hanging about what might have been.
rd.option.continue_quit: Continuing may mean staying true to what you started and avoiding loss, yet it may mean that what drains you stays; stopping may open a new door, yet it carries a fear that it is a hasty decision.
rd.fear.regret_both: That is why the fear of regret takes two opposite shapes here: regret if you go ahead, and regret if you hold back. When regret is possible in every direction, it stops being evidence for any particular one, and becomes a sign that the decision matters to you.
rd.fear.regret: It seems that the fear of regret is strongly present in your words; and perhaps the deeper fear is not of a particular outcome, but of blaming yourself later for not choosing carefully enough.
rd.fear.loss: Perhaps the deeper fear is losing someone you feel close to, or losing the picture you had drawn of what the relationship could become.
rd.fear.people: It seems that how others see you is present in your calculations; that is understandable, but it helps to tell apart what you yourself truly fear from what is only an echo of what people might say.
rd.fear.failure: The fear here may run deeper than a single result: a fear of what the result will say about you, as if failure — if it happened — would become a verdict on your worth rather than on one attempt.
rd.fear.livelihood: It seems that your silence is not weakness, but a reckoning for your livelihood and stability; and that reckoning is legitimate and understandable. Yet long silence about something that keeps happening has a price too: from your peace of mind, and from your sense of your own worth and of the fairness of what you live.
rd.fear.security: Part of the worry may be about security: about being able to meet needs and keep life stable. It is a legitimate worry that needs a realistic reckoning, neither ignoring nor exaggerating.
rd.fear.past: Perhaps the present fear carries the echo of a past experience; whoever has been hurt before becomes cautious, and that caution sometimes protects them, and sometimes makes them see the past in every new situation.
rd.dist.power: There is a difference between an emotional confrontation and wisely claiming what is right; the latter may mean documenting what happens, choosing the right time and the right channel, and calm wording that protects your right without exposing you to needless loss.
rd.dist.income: There is an important difference between a limited income and a lack of stability; the first is a condition that can change through effort and shared planning, while the second concerns seriousness and a clear view of the future. It may be more useful to look at how responsibility is carried than at what is owned right now.
rd.dist.comfort: There is a difference between feeling at ease and being compatible: feeling at ease is an important sign not to be dismissed, while compatibility shows in values, in how disagreements are handled and in how daily life is seen. The first does not replace checking the second, just as nothing makes up for its absence.
rd.dist.family: Your family's reservations may come from their care for you more than from rejecting your choice; understanding exactly where those reservations come from — one specific thing or several — may change the whole shape of the decision, and turn disagreement into dialogue.
rd.dist.pressure: There is a difference between choosing freely and choosing under pressure: the pressure of time, of age, or of insistence from those around you. A decision made to escape pressure may bring relief for a while, but one made from conviction lasts longer.
rd.dist.desire: It seems that in this situation there is a distance between what you want and what others expect of you; acknowledging that distance clearly is the first step toward closing it, rather than letting it remain a silent struggle inside you.
rd.dist.evidence: It matters to tell apart the fear of making a mistake from evidence that a choice is wrong; the first is a natural feeling that accompanies every important decision, and the second is information that deserves to be examined calmly.
rd.dist.guilt: There is a difference between guilt that says “I did wrong” and pushes toward repair, and shame that says “I am bad” and paralyses; the first is a door to repentance and change, while the second only makes the situation heavier.
rd.dist.identity: It matters to separate what happened from your worth; the situation — however hard — describes an experience or a stage, and it cannot serve as a final verdict on you.
rd.dist.forgive: There is a difference between forgiveness and reconciliation: forgiveness frees your heart from the weight of what happened, while reconciliation is a return to the relationship that needs new trust and guarantees. The first may be possible even when the second is not wise.
rd.dist.harm: It matters to tell apart patience with a passing difficulty from staying under ongoing harm; patience is a virtue, but it does not mean accepting what threatens your safety or your dignity.
rd.dist.boundaries: There is a difference between setting clear boundaries and cutting the relationship off; healthy boundaries may be exactly what keeps a relationship from wearing away, not what destroys it.
rd.dist.care: There is a difference between caring for someone you love and carrying everything for them; care that drains you completely cannot last, and asking for help is part of care itself, not a failure in it.
rd.dist.sadness: It matters to tell sadness apart from despair: sadness is pain over what was lost, and it can live alongside hope, while despair passes judgment on the whole future from a single moment.
rd.dist.anger: The anger that shows in your words may be covering something deeper: a wound, a feeling of not being valued, or disappointment in someone from whom you expected otherwise.
rd.dist.suspicion: There is a difference between what you actually saw and what worry fills the gaps with; suspicion feeds on possibilities, and calm checking or direct conversation is more useful than building judgments on them.
rd.dist.lonely: There is a difference between being alone and feeling lonely; the second means missing someone who understands you, and it is a legitimate need for closeness, not a flaw in you.
rd.dist.compare: Comparing yourself with others sets the shop window of their lives against every detail of yours; that is why it is rarely fair, and rarely tells you anything true about your own path.
rd.dist.rest: It matters to tell laziness apart from exhaustion; what looks like falling short may in truth be energy that has been drained, and rest here is not a luxury but a condition for carrying on.
rd.dist.control: There is a difference between what you can influence and what is not in your hands; worry tries to control everything, while calm begins when energy is directed to the part that can actually be done.
rd.dist.facts: It helps to separate what actually happened from your reading of what is in other people's hearts; your reading may be right, but it remains a possibility until it is confirmed.
rd.dist.attach: The attachment to what was — or to what you hoped it would be — may be stronger than the attachment to the person; telling the two apart helps you understand what you truly need now.
rd.dist.griefguilt: Loss is often accompanied by a feeling of having fallen short; but what you see clearly now, after the absence, was not as clear at the time. The shortcoming that pains you is a sign of how much you loved, and the door of kindness through prayer, charity and loyalty is still open.
rd.dist.duty: There is a difference between dutiful kindness to a parent and constant physical presence; kindness has room for many forms of care, contact and practical arrangement, and the more precise thing is to look at what the person you love truly needs, and what can be arranged so it reaches them in every case.
rd.dist.intent: There is a difference between your intention and the effect of your action on the other person; the intention may be sound and the effect painful, and repair begins with acknowledging the effect without needing to deny the intention.
rd.emoFrame: Beneath the surface of what you feel: {0}
rd.close.dilemma_regret: The fear of regret does not mean that either option is wrong. Clarity does not come from erasing this fear, but from knowing what you cannot give up, and what can be built over time.
rd.close.dilemma: Having good reasons in both directions does not make the choice impossible; it means it needs ordering: knowing which of these reasons weighs most for you in the long run, not only in the moment of worry.
rd.close.deciding: Clarity may not come all at once; many decisions become clear step by step, as information is gathered, trustworthy hearts are consulted and Allah's guidance is sought through istikhara, and then the heart is left to settle.
rd.close.harm: Your safety and your dignity are not up for bargaining; any decision you make deserves to start from a safe place, with the support of trusted people or a specialised service, not from a feeling that you face everything alone.
rd.close.wronged: Acknowledging that what happened was painful does not mean you must respond right away or forgive right away; you may take your time, and choose what protects both your dignity and your inner peace.
rd.close.anxious: What awaits you is not a test of your worth, but one station among many; and the more your attention returns to the step in front of you now, the lighter the weight of what has not yet happened becomes.
rd.close.sad: You do not need to find a complete explanation for what you feel in order to deserve gentleness; taking care of yourself in this phase, and coming close to someone you trust, are two steps that come before any deeper understanding.
rd.close.lonely: The need for closeness is not weakness, but part of human nature; the way out of loneliness may begin with one small connection built gently, not with changing everything at once.
rd.close.grieving: Grief for someone lost is not something to get over quickly; it comes to be carried differently with time. What you feel now is not weakness, but the trace of a real love still looking for its place.
rd.close.erred: Admitting the mistake — as your words show — is not the end of the story but its most honest beginning; what matters now is not self-punishment, but one sincere step of repair that opens the door to what follows.
rd.close.carer: Your giving has great value, but it needs protecting too; caring for yourself is not selfishness, it is what makes it possible to keep on giving.
rd.close.worried: Your worry is a sign of your love, but love does its work best when it becomes calm presence and possible steps, not carrying every possibility at once.
rd.close.burden: What you need now may not be a big solution, but a small space to catch your breath; things that look impossible at the peak of exhaustion often become clearer after a little rest and support.
rd.close.self: Your worth is not measured by one situation or one result; and when the picture you hold of yourself is separated from the noise of the moment, dealing with the situation itself becomes much lighter.
rd.close.ghurba: Belonging is not confined to one place; it can be built in the new place little by little without cancelling loyalty to your roots, and every small connection you build here takes nothing away from your love for what you left there.
rd.close.transition: Adapting does not happen all at once; it is made of small days one after another, and what seems strange today may become familiar before you notice.
rd.close.emergency: The priority now is clear practical steps, one after another; and once it has passed, it helps to give yourself time to recover from what you went through, rather than carrying on as if nothing had happened.
rd.close.digital: What happened can be dealt with through practical steps one after another; regaining control begins with one small, clear step, and with remembering that what someone else does does not define your worth.
rd.close.boundaries: Clear boundaries do not make you any less loving or any less generous; they make what you give come from a free choice, not from a sense of being forced.
rd.close.work: Knowing precisely where the pressure comes from is half the way; what is solved by conversation differs from what is solved by boundaries, and both differ from what needs a bigger change.
rd.close.money: Financial strain — however heavy — eases when it turns from a general worry into numbers and clear steps; organised effort together with trust in Allah brings back some calm even before circumstances change.
rd.close.conflict: Close relationships are not measured by the absence of conflict, but by the ability to repair what cracks in them; repair often begins with one calm sentence at the right time.
rd.close.parenting: Children's behaviour is usually a message about a need they have not found words for; combining firmness with warmth, with patience for gradual change, makes a bigger difference than any single day shows.
rd.close.faith: The door of returning to Allah is never closed, and the way to Him is travelled by small, steady steps more than by big, broken leaps; the unease you feel is a sign that you are still on the path.
rd.close.health: Caring for the emotional side is part of the journey of treatment, not a luxury; anything that eases your load — company, rest or clear information — deserves to be given its place.
rd.close.habit: Change here rarely comes from one big decision, but from a small change in environment, timing and alternatives, repeated until it becomes a new habit.
rd.close.general: Calmly understanding what is happening inside you is the first step; many situations become lighter when their feelings and needs are named clearly, before looking for any solution.
